title: kernel_worklist — the ranked, bucketed candidate list
description:
`items/text.json` of the `kernel_worklist` handoff: which kernels are worth an optimisation attempt, and **why the rest are not**. Written against the real sealed artefact at `cheat_for_mock/stage3-analyze/kernel_worklist/` (34 kernels, five buckets).

The sealed artefact already carries a schema at `items/schema`, and that one is the reason this one exists: every interior is `{"type": "object"}`, so it accepts a `buckets` with no shares in it and a `kernels` row that is selected and excluded at the same time. A schema that validates everything is worse than no schema, because it passes and nobody looks again.

What this adds over that one, and each is a rule the previous round relied on and did not check:

1. **Selection and exclusion are a biconditional.** A row is selected with a rank and no reason, or unselected with a reason and no rank. Both halves were representable before.
2. **The bucket names are the taxonomy**, closed. `assets/lib/kernel_taxonomy.yaml` sorts first-match-wins into exactly these five, and a sixth in the document means the taxonomy and the ranker disagree about what a bucket is.
3. **Every bucket accounts for itself** — a count and a share, so `check_worklist_shape` can add the shares and compare against the profile.
4. **`source` records what was ranked**, by sha256 and row count. A worklist whose provenance is a filename is a worklist that cannot be told apart from one built over a different capture — and the mock set contains exactly that trap: two artefacts under the name `kernel_table`, one a real 124-kernel capture and one a 34-row synthetic seed.

What a schema cannot do and `check_worklist_shape` therefore does: add `buckets[].pct_total` and check the total accounts for the run, and check `summary` against the actual contents of `kernels`. Arithmetic over a document is not expressible here and pretending otherwise would leave it unchecked in both places.

schema_version.description: The one field this schema requires that the sealed artefact does not carry. It is added rather than dropped: an unversioned structured document is one that cannot be migrated, and every other schema in this package carries it.

source.description: What was ranked. Identity by digest and not by name, for the reason in the header.

enriched.description: Whether the table carried launcher/Python-frame columns beyond Magpie's own.

launchers.description: Whether any kernel could be tied to a Python frame, and if not, why not. Recorded rather than inferred from an empty result: 'the profiler did not record frames' and 'the frames were recorded and matched nothing' are different facts and only one of them is a defect.

thresholds.description: The knobs the ranking was run at. Present so that a worklist with two candidates can be told apart from a profile with two candidates — `top_n: 2` explains the first and nothing explains the second.

environment.description: A summary for a reader of this document alone. **Not** the environment record: that is `items/env/environment.yaml`, it validates against `environment.schema.json`, and `check_environment` grades it. Two documents because this one is a legend and that one is a contract.

buckets.description: One entry per taxonomy bucket present in the ranking. Closed, and the five names are `assets/lib/kernel_taxonomy.yaml`'s. `vendor_tuned` is excluded wholesale today — right for a first pass and wrong in general, since a vendor kernel can be beaten on a shape the vendor did not tune for; that is `todo.md` T2 and it is deferred, not forgotten.

kernels.description: **Every kernel the ranking saw**, selected or not. Not the candidates: the candidates are the subset with `selected: true`. Carrying the rejected rows with their reasons is what makes the exclusions reviewable, and 63% of profiled GPU time in this capture is in rows that will never be selected.

pct_total.description: Share of profiled GPU time. The 100.5 ceiling rather than 100 allows for rounding across rows; above it something is being double-counted across ranks.

kernel_id.description: Stable within one worklist and the join key every later artefact uses — `operator_identity.operators[].kernel_id` and `workset.operators[].kernel_id` are this.

name.description: The device symbol exactly as the profiler recorded it, parenthesised template arguments included. Not normalised: a normalised symbol cannot be matched back against the trace.

input_shapes.description: Magpie's `Input Shapes` cell, verbatim and unparsed. Populated only when the capture asked for `record_shapes`; empty here means every roofline downstream is impossible, and it is the one absence nothing else would notice.

bucket.description: Which of the four taxonomy buckets this kernel fell in, from `assets/lib/kernel_taxonomy.yaml`, plus `unknown` for a symbol no rule matched. **`routable` below is derived from this and is not a second predicate** — `taxonomy.bucket_of` reads the bucket's own `routable` flag, and measured against the taxonomy, exactly one bucket carries it: the one named `routable`. So `bucket == 'routable'` and `routable == true` are the same statement, bound by `allOf` below so they cannot drift apart. m4 asked whether these were one predicate or two and could not tell, because this description did not exist — the absence was the finding.

routable.description: Whether an optimiser could act on this kernel at all. **Derived from `bucket`, never set independently** — true exactly when `bucket` is `routable`. Kept as its own field because a consumer filtering the candidate pool should not have to know which bucket name means 'routable'; bound to `bucket` so the convenience cannot become a disagreement.

category.description: The operator family — `moe_gemm`, `attention`, `norm`, … `unknown` when the taxonomy has no rule for it, which is a gap in the rule table and is recorded as one (`todo.md` T4).

cases.description: The distinct shapes observed for this kernel, deduplicated. The seed of `workset.operators[].shapes`, and the reason M3.7.4.1's '≥3' is checkable this early: a candidate with one observed shape is one whose speedup claim will be about one shape.

selector.description: An **identity for the case, not a statement about the GEMM**. The M/K/N are derived mechanically from the raw shape tuple and the sealed artefact's own note says so in as many words: N there is `model_dim//2`, not the GEMM's N. Build tensors from the axes; use this only to select.

allOf.$comment: Selection and exclusion are one decision recorded in three fields, so they are constrained together. A selected row with a reason, or an unselected row without one, was representable in the sealed artefact's own schema and is what `check_worklist_shape`'s brief means by 'every exclusion carries a reason'.
A non-routable kernel cannot be a candidate. The converse does not hold: routable-but-below-threshold is the normal case.
